name: Pharaoh
overview: Pharaoh was the male ruler of Egypt at the time of Moses' birth, as noted in Exodus 1:11. He is a significant figure in the early Exodus narrative. This Pharaoh died before Moses returned from his exile in Midian, according to Exodus 2:23. His identity is primarily defined by his role during this critical period in Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: The title 'Pharaoh' is used to refer to this ruler, as recorded in Exodus 1:11. Additionally, he is called the 'King of Egypt,' which simply denotes his position as the sovereign of Egypt (Exodus 1:15). Neither title is given by God, but both emphasize his earthly authority.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for this Pharaoh beyond his role during Moses' birth and the time before Moses' return from exile. There are no further personal or familial details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: This Pharaoh is significant as the reigning king during the early oppression of the Israelites in Egypt, setting the stage for God's deliverance through Moses. His death before Moses' return marks a transition point in the narrative, allowing for the unfolding of God's redemptive plan for His people. The biblical account highlights his role as a temporal authority whose reign is ultimately subordinate to God's sovereign purposes.
